items.name: API client base + backend error-code localization
items.description: Confirm HttpRequest/Interceptors are the single API surface, set the base URL from VITE_APP_API_URL, and add a typed map from the backend's machine-readable error codes to localized messages.
acceptance: VITE_APP_API_URL documented in .env.example
A typed EApiErrorCode enum covering at least GAS_OUT_OF_RANGE, ENTRANTS_STILL_INSIDE, CERT_EXPIRED, FIRE_WATCH_NOT_ELAPSED
A composable or util maps an error response {code, ...} to a localized string via i18n; unknown codes fall back to a generic localized message and are console.error'd
Backend message strings are never rendered directly

Unit test: known code → localized string; unknown code → fallback
./init.sh green
items.notes: DONE except one MANUAL step. useApiError() returns { mapError(error) => { code, message, isKnown, details } } — message is ALWAYS the localized string; the backend raw message is never rendered. Unknown/network/timeout errors fall back to error.unknown AND console.error the real error (never swallowed). code is typed as plain string, not the enum, so unknown future codes still typecheck. HttpRequest.ts and Interceptors.ts were NOT touched — the base-URL seam already exists (HttpRequest.ts:37 reads import.meta.env.VITE_APP_API_URL with a || fallback, EnvChecker.ts asserts it), so pointing at a real backend is already a one-line change. || MANUAL STEP FOR THE USER: .env.example still lists a dead VITE_APP_WEBSOCKET (zero references left in the repo since useSocket.ts was deleted in PLT-001). Neither the agent nor the orchestrator can edit it — a global deny rule Read(**/.env*) blocks Read/Write/Bash on that path, and bypassing it was declined as a deliberate security boundary. The user must delete that one line by hand.
